alert_unknown_entity_references.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your alerts 👻

The alert {alert} (`{entity_id}`) watches an entity that is unknown to Home Assistant:

{entities}

An alert can only fire on the entity it watches, so this one can never fire again. It looks the same as an alert with nothing to report.

To fix this error, edit the `alert:` section in your configuration and point this alert at an entity that exists.

Spook 👻 Your homie.
alert_unknown_entity_references.title: Unknown entity watched by alert: {alert}

alert_unknown_notifiers.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your alerts 👻

The alert {alert} (`{entity_id}`) notifies through the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{notifiers}

The alert still fires and still does its rounds, but these notifications go nowhere. Home Assistant logs that only at the moment the alert fires, which is a poor moment to find out nobody is listening.

To fix this error, edit the `notifiers:` list of this alert in your configuration and remove or correct these entries.

Spook 👻 Your homie.
alert_unknown_notifiers.title: Unknown notifiers used by alert: {alert}

notify_unknown_group_members.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your notify groups 👻

The notify group `{group}` forwards to the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{members}

The group still delivers to the rest of its members, and it still reports success to whatever called it, so nothing upstream notices. The failure surfaces only as a stray "Task exception was never retrieved" in the log, which names no group and reads like a bug. Whoever was behind that member simply stops being notified.

To fix this error, edit the `services:` list of this group in your configuration and remove or correct these entries.

Spook 👻 Your homie.
notify_unknown_group_members.title: Unknown members in notify group: {group}
